# TORQUEBAY: the racer template (NetNet game runtime, play style "racer")

> Kart races for up to 8 players on harbour circuits, with seat bots filling
> the grid. A round is one race of a few laps; the next round runs another
> circuit. You change the game by editing src/game.ts only. The template
> already has the kart physics (throttle, brakes, steering, grip, drift
> mini-turbos in three tiers, boost pads, coins that raise top speed, grass,
> barriers, kart bumps), laps through ordered checkpoints, the race clock and
> places, bots that drive the racing line, netcode with client prediction at
> 60 Hz, a streamed track (only the road near you is built), rendering in
> every art style, keyboard, gamepad and touch controls, earn and the store.
> Do not write renderers, netcode, physics or bot AI.

## Files

- src/game.ts: THE GAME. Declarations against @netforge/engine:
  game(), upgrade(), system(), earn.rule(), earn.stake(), store.sku().
- src/names.json: the title and every label players read.
- Everything else is template machinery.

## Rules the build enforces

- game({ template: "racer", style: "lowpoly", tracks: [...] }) with 1 to 8 tracks.
- No weapon(), director(), keeper() or enemy prefabs.
- A track has 4 to 64 control points at least 6 m apart and is at least 200 m round.
- Asset ids look like "style.lowpoly.kart_a", never URLs or paths, and must be in the asset library.
- game({ style }) is the art style the creator picked: lowpoly, toon, ps1, pixel, voxel or handdrawn. Keep it.
- Ids are lower_snake_case. Every game declares at least one earn.rule and one earn.stake (the buy-in run).
- Upgrades raise one of: speed (top speed), haste (drift charge rate), might
  (boost length), armor (grass and wall losses), magnet (coin reach, m).
- 4 players plus seat bots must all finish a race, and an earn rule must
  fire, in a 4-minute playtest.

## Units

Seconds, metres, metres per second. The ground plane: x and z in metres.
Tick rate 60 Hz. Default top speed 26 m/s; a kart is about 1.8 m long.

## The loop

Everyone lines up on a staggered grid behind the line. A 3 s countdown, then
the race: W/Up accelerate, S/Down brake, A/D steer, hold Space or Shift
while steering through a bend to drift (sparks turn blue, orange, then
purple as the mini-turbo charges; release for a 0.5, 0.9 or 1.4 s boost).
Boost pads boost; each coin held adds 1% top speed, up to 10. Grass slows,
barriers bounce. Laps count through four quarter checkpoints in order. The
round closes 25 s after the first person finishes (or at round.seconds);
the results show, then the next circuit.

## Building a track

tracks: [{
  name: "Harbour Loop",
  laps: 3,
  width: 14,                                 // asphalt, m (8 to 30)
  points: [[0, 0], [90, 0], [150, 15], ...], // the closed centreline in driving order; a smooth curve runs through them
  boosts: [[0.12, 0], [0.47, -0.4]],         // [lap fraction 0..1, lateral -1 (left) .. 1 (right)]
  coins: [[0.04, 0.5], [0.046, 0.5]],        // same coordinates; each kart collects its own (at most 62)
  verge: 4,                                  // optional grass before the barrier, m
}]
Rules of thumb: 500 to 900 m a lap at 14 m wide runs 25 to 40 s a lap; keep
neighbouring points 20 m or more apart for smooth bends; a hairpin needs
about 25 m of radius; put boosts on the exits of bends and coin rows on the
racing line or slightly off it (a choice). Two to four laps a race.

## Common changes

### A new circuit
Add a track to tracks. Circuits come one a round (the room draws one per round).

### Tune the handling
kart: { topSpeed: 30, turn: 2.6, grip: 10, driftGrip: 1.5 } (topSpeed 10-45,
accel 8-80, turn 1-4, grip 3-20, driftGrip 0.5-6, grass 0.2-1, boostSpeed 1-1.8).

### Round length and bots
round: { seconds: 240 } (60 to 600). players.bots: 6 fills the grid up to 6
with seat bots (0 turns them off). Bots drive the racing line, shaded by
skill, never earn, and a win over a field of bots pays nothing extra.

### Add an earn rule
earn.rule("lap_leader", { when: "lap.completed", n: 2, pay: 3, oncePer: "run" });
Events: player.finished (you finished the race), race.won (first, paid only
with another person in the round), race.podium (top three, same),
lap.completed, coin.collected, drift.boosted (a mini-turbo fired),
drift.ultra (a full-charge one), kart.bumped (a hard wall hit),
round.finished, run.started (unpaid), and anything you emit(). Each rule
pays once per race per player, in coins; the room server is the referee.

### Track something with a system
system("clean_line", ({ on, emit }) => {
  const scrapes = new Map<number, number>();
  on("kart.bumped", (ids) => { for (const id of ids) scrapes.set(id, (scrapes.get(id) ?? 0) + 1); });
  on("player.finished", (ids) => { const clean = ids.filter((id) => !scrapes.get(id)); if (clean.length) emit("race.clean", clean); });
  on("run.started", (ids) => { for (const id of ids) scrapes.delete(id); });
});
Systems also have every, after, onTick, players(), random(), announce(text),
upcoming(label, seconds) and end(). spawn and enemies are not part of this template.

### The buy-in run (required)
earn.stake({ min: 10, max: 100, multiple: 2 }); one top-level line. "stake" is reserved.

### Losable gear (optional)
store.sku("bumper_kit", { coins: 120, grants: { gear: "bumpers", loseBelow: 0.25 } });
Owned in the profile, coins only; one level of its upgrade in every staked
race; lost when that race makes less than loseBelow of its most earn.

### Coins: earn and the store
store.sku("turbo", { coins: 40 });                               // one level of the "turbo" upgrade for the race
store.sku("skin_flame", { coins: 300, grants: { cosmetic: 1 } }); // a paint job, owned for good
Keep the five SKUs the client is wired to (turbo, tuned_engine, soft_tyres,
skin_flame, skin_chrome) at their prices, with the paints' grants (flame 1,
chrome 2). PvP pots are not part of this template.

### Change the karts (the asset library)
players: { prefab: "style.lowpoly.race_car", ... } (any vehicle: kart_a..e,
race_car, race_car_future, buggy-like speeder_a..c). Seat bots drive
kart_b..e; the pixel style draws its own kart sprites.

## Test

engine.test.run({ ticks: 60 * 240, bots: 4, assert: [...] }) runs races on
the server sim with 4 playtest drivers plus seat bots and reports rounds
(wave), runs.won (races every playtest driver finished), scorers (drivers
that finished at least once), deaths (hard wall hits), earned by rule,
softlock and ms per tick.
